sites.corridor_fit: The officially signed I-10 routing through downtown Los Angeles: the San Bernardino Freeway S-10 section plus the I-10/US-101 concurrency between the San Bernardino terminus and the Santa Monica Freeway origin - the same unsigned-concurrency class as the Memphis (218838) and Denver (59709) dispositions.
sites.direction_review: Milepost-directed at both boundaries: US-101 mp 0.0 begins at the Santa Monica Freeway break end and increases toward the San Bernardino junction; S-10 mp 16.24-17.012 continues into the locked component-0 records at 17.012. Every internal join is an exact shared coordinate (0.0 m). Acquisition adds route-family candidates only - the westbound directed edge selection remains the later solve, which may reject any of them.
sites.evidence_summary: Geometric probe: a 22-record undirected S-10/U-101 path exists. Census: exact 0.0 m same-key joins; the eastern end continues as S-10 on the segment's own LRS key 000000001001037. Interior sweep: both downtown interiors carry I-5/US-101/S-60 records on the straight chord while the S-10 records cross it at 77-82 degrees (the mainline curves away from the chord). NHS: CA route SHS_010._P signed I-10/S-10 with continuous measures 15.824-17.572 across the site.
sites.resolution: 2026-08-31 directed whole-key milepost review of S-10 key 000000001001037 (417 records, unfiltered) plus the unfiltered exact-join walk across the void: the S-10 San Bernardino chain is milepost-contiguous 16.24-17.012 and joins the locked component-0 start (546553, mp 17.012) at 0.0 m, but the key's milepost space jumps one source quantum (16.239 to 16.24) across 2,112.6 m of pavement the key does not carry. That stretch is the signed I-10/US-101 downtown concurrency: US-101 key 000000010101037 begins (mp 0.0, record 546519) exactly at the locked Santa Monica Freeway chain end (546512, mp 16.239) with a 0.0 m join, runs milepost-contiguous 0.0-1.28 with exact joins throughout, and its junction records 546569/546559 meet the S-10 chain start (546568, mp 16.24) at 0.0 m. The 23-record set (9 S-10 + 14 US-101) is the unique exact-join freeway chain between the locked ends; the alternates through the interchange are I-5/S-60/local-street records that do not carry the signed I-10 routing. Candidates only; the westbound directed edge selection remains the later solve.

sites.resolution: 2026-08-31 sliver acquisition and geometric review: OBJECTID 38597 (S-95 key MOHAVEVAHW08015, mp 0-0.015, 14.1 m) runs exactly from one locked I-40 chain end (38590, I-40 mp 115.481) to the other (38595, I-40/S-95 mp 0.23) with 0.0 m endpoint offsets at both ends and 0.0 m line offsets - the record's whole extent IS the 14.069 m gap pavement at the S-95 terminus. Its neighbour 38596 (mp 0.015-0.046) tees away north on S-95 and is not corridor pavement, which is what the census's ~88-degree grading measured. Of the three listed mechanisms, sliver acquisition of 38597 alone is exact and minimal: NHS fill would substitute a supplementary source where NHPN itself asserts the joining pavement, and a bounded exception would author what the source already carries.

sites.blocking_question: The anchor sits mid-record on the corridor's own locked pavement (433412), so no acquisition can bring a graph node within the 25 m anchor limit. sites.evidence_summary: The locked from-anchor sits 381.157 m from any candidate endpoint - a transfer-anchor mismatch, not a road break; the geometric probe found the anchor outside the local source graph (4 features, no path). Census: the segment's Jersey City approach ends join US-22 (427523) and an NJ-139-key record (434168). NHS: NJ I-78 (00000078__) continuous 66.339-67.16 through the anchor window.
sites.mechanism_review: 2026-08-31 measure review: the anchor lies exactly on locked record 433412 (Holland Tunnel, 1,576 m) at line offset 0.0 m, 381.157 m from that record's nearest endpoint. No record in the unfiltered 500 m envelope - locked or unlocked - has an endpoint within the 25 m anchor snap limit (nearest unlocked endpoint: 433415 at 381.2 m), so approach-record acquisition cannot resolve this site. The remaining mechanisms are transfer-lock-affecting: re-derive the anchor onto a candidate endpoint, or teach the edge-path solve to split an edge at an on-edge anchor.

sites.evidence_summary: Both probes agree the 1.011 m Omaha pair is milepost-contiguous and joined by nothing: no third feature exists in the source, and the nearest other features are a US-275/S-92 crossing ~470 m away. The gap is 11 mm beyond the locked 1 m endpoint tolerance and sits inside the 1.61 m milepost quantum. NHS: NE route 080 (I-80) continuous 445.05-445.48 across the point.

exception.rationale: The source asserts adjacency in linear referencing (one record's END_POINT equals the other's BEGIN_POIN on the same key) while authoring no joining geometry; no acquisition can close it. A deterministic ADR-0018 authored overlay bounded to this 1.011 m span closes it without widening the 1 m snap tolerance, which stays unchanged.

NHS: IL I-80 (037  10080 000000) 3.91-5.52 and I-74 continuous across the site.

exception.rationale: Acquiring the joining I-74/I-280 records cannot close the break - they carry the same 9.190 m discontinuity, which is why the unfiltered local graph finds no path. The source asserts milepost adjacency across the gap; a deterministic ADR-0018 authored overlay bounded to this 9.190 m span is the only closure. The 1 m snap tolerance stays unchanged.
